It's really only the fans, vents, and heatsinks that collect dust. Also the power supply (fan). You just unplug the power, crack open the case, remove the fans, and wipe everything down with a paper towel. Then give it a second wipedown with towel soaked in alcohol (no water) and a quick wipe over the motherboard. (Make sure you wait awhile before powering PC back on; otherwise, you'll short your motherboard.) Use cotton swabs for the tight crevices. Use Scotch tape to lift up the layer of dust on the motherboard, and cover any open PCI/RAM slots with tape. Don't remove the heatsink from the CPU unless you have a tube of thermal paste to use on the bottom again. If your old paste is dried, your CPU won't be flush with the heatsink anymore and your temps will spike as soon as you boot. However, you should replace the thermal paste every 3-4 years anyway.
